gen-gf-grandstander-gf-anek-latin: Anek Latin reads with lowercase that nearly reaches the capitals, its rounds held open rather than curled shut. Grandstander is the one to make noise with its fat, uniform strokes; the body font simply keeps going.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-anek-malayalam: Chunky, bendy and loud, this heading looks like pipe twisted into letters. gen-gf-grandstander-gf-anek-odia: Stitched-thread strokes, all one weight, give Grandstander a playful, hand-bent look. Anek Odia answers in a plain sans whose rounds stay unlatched, like hooks, and whose capitals rise only slightly above the lowercase.

gen-gf-grandstander-gf-anuphan: Bold and a bit cheeky, Grandstander looks like neatly bent pipe cleaner, with short ascenders and a tall x-height. Anuphan takes the quieter job in a sans, its big round bowls and open curves with clear gaps carrying the text.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-arimo: Grandstander looks like spaghetti laid out in letters, every stroke the same width, with short ascenders and a tall x-height. Arimo follows in a sans with a tall mean line, and a long passage would flow easily.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-armata: Springy, hairline-free letters with no swells anywhere make Grandstander look like it was bent by hand. Armata keeps a long passage moving in a plain sans, with spacious gaps between characters and rounded glyphs left open at the terminals.
